title: Human metapneumovirus infection in hospitalized children: a four-year retrospective study from a tertiary pediatric hospital
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important viral cause of acute respiratory infections, particularly in young children, and may lead to hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease. However, detailed clinical data from hospitalized pediatric cohorts remain limited. This study combined two complementary datasets from a tertiary pediatric hospital in Palermo, Italy. The hospital microbiology dataset included all PCR-confirmed hMPV detections recorded from October 2021 to May 2025 ( n = 636, including 560 pediatric cases) and was used only to describe temporal distribution. The clinical cohort comprised 78 of the pediatric cases who were hospitalized in the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit between January 2022 and May 2025 and had complete clinical records. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, and therapeutic data were collected and analyzed through IBM SPSS Statistics using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses. Continuous variables were summarized as median and interquartile range (IQR), while categorical variables were reported as absolute frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between children who received antibiotics and those who did not were performed using Pearson’s chi-square or exact tests, as appropriate. Associations between categorical predictors and length of hospital stay were explored using the Mann–Whitney U test. Correlation with age was assessed using Spearman’s coefficient. The median age of hospitalized children was 14 months (IQR 3–30). The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. Chest X-ray was performed in 41 (52.6%) patients and showed abnormal findings in all cases, most commonly consolidation patterns. Viral coinfections were detected in 25.6% of patients, and bacterial organisms were detected in 24.4%. Oxygen support was required in 60.3% of cases, and five patients (6.4%) required pediatric intensive care admission. Antibiotics were prescribed in 70.5% of patients, although bacterial organisms were detected in only 24.4%. Our findings describe the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with hMPV infection in a tertiary pediatric center, highlighting the clinical relevance of hMPV among hospitalized children in our center. Moreover, the high rate of antibiotic prescription observed in this cohort highlights the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing viral from bacterial respiratory infections and underscores the importance of improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease.

The research highlights the importance of hMPV as a cause of acute respiratory infections in young children, particularly those requiring hospitalization. The study combined two datasets, one describing the temporal distribution of hMPV infections and the other focusing on clinical data from 78 hospitalized cases. Key findings include the high prevalence of symptoms such as cough, fever, and respiratory distress, as well as the frequent use of antibiotics despite limited bacterial coinfections. However, the study is limited by its retrospective design and potential selection bias, as it included only a subset of cases with complete records, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人偏肺病毒(hMPV)是急性呼吸道感染的重要病原体,尤其是在婴幼儿中,可能导致下呼吸道疾病住院。然而,关于住院儿科患者人偏肺病毒感染的详细临床数据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究结合了意大利巴勒莫一家三级儿科医院的两个互补数据集。临床数据集包括2022年1月至2025年5月期间在儿科感染性疾病病房住院的78例儿科病例,这些病例具有完整的临床记录。
elements_zh.methods: 通过IBM SPSS Statistics收集和分析了人口学、临床、实验室、影像学和治疗数据,采用描述性统计和探索性双变量分析。连续变量以中位数和四分位数范围(IQR)进行总结,而分类变量则以绝对频数和百分比进行报告。使用Pearson卡方检验或精确检验(根据情况)比较接受抗生素治疗和未接受抗生素治疗的儿童。
elements_zh.main_results: 最常见的临床表现和症状包括咳嗽(64例;82.1%)、发热(59例;75.6%)以及呼吸窘迫迹象,包括呼吸急促(48例;61.5%)和肋间凹陷(38例;48.7%)。食欲减退(32例;41%)和流涕(29例;37.2%)也较为常见。41例(52.6%)患者进行了胸部X光检查,所有病例均显示异常结果,最常见的异常为肺实变。25.6%的患者检测到病毒合并感染,24.4%检测到细菌病原体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的研究结果描述了在三级儿科中心住院的人偏肺病毒感染儿童的临床特征和管理情况,突显了人偏肺病毒在我们中心住院儿童中的临床重要性。此外,本研究中观察到的高抗生素处方率突显了在区分病毒性与细菌性呼吸道感染方面的诊断挑战,并强调了在儿科呼吸道疾病中改善抗菌药物使用和病毒学监测的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以谨慎地用于改善儿科呼吸道疾病中的抗菌药物使用和病毒学监测,强调了需要更好的诊断工具来区分病毒性与细菌性感染在住院儿童中的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和可能的选择偏倚,因为仅包括了78例具有完整临床记录的住院儿科病例。由于样本量有限以及仅关注单一三级儿科中心,证据强度中等。

The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. Chest X-ray was performed in 41 (52.6%) patients and showed abnormal findings in all cases, most commonly consolidation patterns. Viral coinfections were detected in 25.6% of patients, and bacterial organisms were detected in 24.4%. Oxygen support was required in 60.3% of cases, and five patients (6.4%) required pediatric intensive care admission. Antibiotics were prescribed in 70.5% of patients, although bacterial organisms were detected in only 24.4%. Our findings describe the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with hMPV infection in a tertiary pediatric center, highlighting the clinical relevance of hMPV among hospitalized children in our center. Moreover, the high rate of antibiotic prescription observed in this cohort highlights the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing viral from bacterial respiratory infections and underscores the importance of improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease.
abstract_zh: 人偏肺病毒(hMPV)是急性呼吸道感染的重要病原体,尤其是在婴幼儿中,可能导致下呼吸道疾病住院。然而,关于住院儿科患者人偏肺病毒感染的详细临床数据仍然有限。本研究结合了意大利巴勒莫一家三级儿科医院的两个互补数据集。医院微生物学数据集包括从2021年10月至2025年5月期间通过PCR确认的所有hMPV检测记录(n=636,其中包含560例儿科病例),仅用于描述时间分布。临床数据集包括2022年1月至2025年5月期间在儿科感染性疾病病房住院的78例儿科病例,这些病例具有完整的临床记录。通过IBM SPSS Statistics收集和分析了人口学、临床、实验室、影像学和治疗数据,采用描述性统计和探索性双变量分析。连续变量以中位数和四分位数范围(IQR)进行总结,而分类变量则以绝对频数和百分比进行报告。使用Pearson卡方检验或精确检验(根据情况)比较接受抗生素治疗和未接受抗生素治疗的儿童。使用Mann–Whitney U检验探索分类预测变量与住院时间之间的关联。使用Spearman系数评估与年龄的相关性。住院儿童的中位年龄为14个月(IQR 3–30)。最常见的临床表现和症状包括咳嗽(64例;82.1%)、发热(59例;75.6%)以及呼吸窘迫迹象,包括呼吸急促(48例;61.5%)和肋间凹陷(38例;48.7%)。食欲减退(32例;41%)和流涕(29例;37.2%)也较为常见。41例(52.6%)患者进行了胸部X光检查,所有病例均显示异常结果,最常见的异常为肺实变。25.6%的患者检测到病毒合并感染,24.4%检测到细菌病原体。60.3%的病例需要氧气支持,其中5例(6.4%)需要儿科重症监护病房入院。尽管仅24.4%的患者检测到细菌病原体,但仍有70.5%的患者开具了抗生素。我们的研究结果描述了在三级儿科中心住院的人偏肺病毒感染儿童的临床特征和管理情况,突显了人偏肺病毒在我们中心住院儿童中的临床重要性。此外,本研究中观察到的高抗生素处方率突显了在区分病毒性与细菌性呼吸道感染方面的诊断挑战,并强调了在儿科呼吸道疾病中改善抗菌药物使用和病毒学监测的重要性。

title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

The evidence highlights the virus's targeting of respiratory epithelium and the immune responses it triggers. elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人偏肺病毒 主要针对呼吸道上皮,触发 免疫应答,从而有助于病毒清除和疾病 发病机制。包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂在内的研究疗法显示出希望,但需要进一步验证。免疫调节剂和草药可能会提供支持性益处,但它们对抗 HMPV 的功效尚未得到证实。疫苗 的开发正在进行中,有几个候选药物处于临床前和早期临床阶段。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该病毒通过多种机制逃避 免疫应答,导致疾病严重化,特别是在弱势群体中。尽管目前支持性护理是主流,但新兴的 抗病毒药物 和 疫苗 可能会提供未来的解决方案。改善诊断途径、公众意识和有针对性的研究对于控制 HMPV 感染至关重要。需要进一步的临床试验来建立安全有效的治疗方案。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。

abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

title: Vaccination in Older Adults with COPD: Preventing Pneumonia, Exacerbations and Hospitalization
abstract: Older adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are particularly vulnerable to respiratory infections because of reduced pulmonary reserve, comorbidity, and age-related changes in immune function. This narrative review examines the role of vaccination in older adults with COPD, focusing on influenza, pneumococcal, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), COVID-19, and other vaccines recommended according to age or individual risk. Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination have the longest-standing COPD-specific evidence, with studies reporting reductions in selected respiratory outcomes and COPD exacerbations. RSV vaccines have shown efficacy against RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease in large trials of older adults, and more recent observational studies in COPD have reported protection against RSV-related hospitalization and severe exacerbations. Data on COVID-19 vaccination in COPD support immunogenicity and acceptable safety, but direct evidence for prevention of COPD exacerbations is limited. For other vaccines, recommendations are based mainly on age and individual risk, with relatively little evidence for COPD-specific clinical outcomes. Vaccination should be considered an important component of preventive care in older adults with COPD, although the evidence supporting individual vaccines differs in both quantity and direct applicability to this population. Important uncertainties remain regarding effects on all-cause exacerbations, hospitalization, mortality, functional outcomes, and the duration of protection.

title: Burden of RSV hospital disease and its comorbidities in adults in Spain (2016-2023).
abstract: This observational descriptive study analyses the hospital burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults in Spain using the Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS) from the Spanish National Hospital Data Surveillance System. Hospital admissions of adults diagnosed with non-bronchiolitis RSV infection between 2016 and 2023 were identified using ICD-10-CM codes. A total of 288,297 RSV-related hospitalizations were recorded, with a mean patient age of 76.18 years. The overall hospitalization rate was 92.43 per 100,000 inhabitants, and the mortality rate was 5.32 per 100,000. The most common severe comorbidities at admission were congestive heart failure, diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Patients aged over 65 years had a significantly higher risk of in-hospital mortality (OR 1.78; 95% CI: 1.64-1.93) compared to those aged 40-64 years, increasing to 2.22 (95% CI: 2.05-2.40) in the presence of at least one severe comorbidity. Male sex was also associated with increased mortality risk (OR 1.24; 95% CI: 1.20-1.28). In conclusion, RSV represents a substantial cause of hospitalization and mortality among adults in Spain, particularly in patients over 60 years, males, and those with underlying comorbidities.

title: RSV vaccine uptake among Medicare Advantage enrollees: August 2023 to December 2024.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the most common causes of respiratory tract infections, disproportionately affecting young children, older adults, and those with chronic medical conditions. In the US, RSV vaccine recommendations by the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) for adults were first issued in 2023 and have since evolved. Uptake of the RSV vaccine by eligible US adults has been slower than expected, with approximately one-fifth (21.0%) of adults aged ≥ 65 years enrolled in Medicare fee-for-service plans receiving the vaccine in the first season of availability. We analyzed RSV vaccine uptake over two seasons among older adults enrolled in Medicare Advantage. Overall RSV vaccine uptake was higher in the 2023/2024 season compared with the 2024/2025 season, peaking in October of both years. Adults ≥ 75 years had higher vaccine uptake than those 65-74 years. Vaccination was highest among groups at increased risk for severe RSV illness. Among approximately 1.7 MM individuals who met the 2024 CDC recommendations for vaccination, roughly 80% did not have evidence of RSV vaccination. Targeted strategies are needed to further reach adults who are at increased risk for severe RSV illness.

title: Safety of nirsevimab in children aged 0-24 months: Analysis based on EudraVigilance data (2023-2025).
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, and it is associated with substantial morbidity, including hospitalization and death. After European Medicine Agency approval of nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody against RSV, immunization campaigns have been implemented in several European Union countries for administration to children as preventive intervention against severe RSV disease during RSV epidemic season. Monitoring its safety in routine healthcare practice is also important. We described suspected adverse drug reactions (ADRs) following nirsevimab administration in children aged 0-24 months, reported in the EudraVigilance system between 2023 and 2025. There were 1,923 ADRs, corresponding to 808 cases. By System Organ Class, ADRs mainly included general disorders and administration site conditions, which include nonspecific systemic manifestations and administration-site reactions that cannot be readily assigned to a single organ system (28.4%), infections and infestations (23.3%), respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal disorders (12.2%); by Preferred Terms most frequent were drug ineffective (12.6%), and RSV bronchiolitis (9.6%). In addition, pyrexia, rash, and injection site reactions were also common. This study offered systematic characterization of ADRs following administration of nirsevimab. It found that the reported ADRs are consistent with the safety results from pre- and real-world safety studies. Our study can support the continue monitoring of the real-world safety and guide the planning of analytical observational studies on the safety profile of nirsevimab.

title: Nirsevimab reduced acute otitis media infections in infants-a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections in young children worldwide. Acute otitis media (AOM) is among the most frequent complications of RSV infection and the leading indication for antibiotic prescribing in this age group. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of nirsevimab in reducing the incidence of AOM among infants. We conducted a nationwide register-based interrupted time-series study using data on live births, laboratory-confirmed RSV detections, and AOM diagnoses from four consecutive RSV seasons (2022-2023 to 2025-2026). Monthly infant populations at risk were reconstructed from birth cohorts to estimate incidence rates during the peak RSV seasons (December-March) which were compared between two pre-implementation and two post-implementation RSV seasons in infants aged < 12 months, stratified into age groups of 0-2, 3-5, and 6-11 months. The study population consisted of 181,999 infants and the follow-up consisted of 2,022,261 infant-months. A total of 3699 RSV-positive findings and 15,830 AOM diagnoses were included in the primary analysis. Following nirsevimab implementation, the incidence of AOM and RSV among infants aged < 12 months decreased by 44% (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.54-0.58) and 83% (RR 0.17, 95% CI 0.15-0.18), respectively. The reduction was greatest in the youngest age (0-2 months) group. CONCLUSION: Implementation of a nirsevimab immunisation programme was associated with a substantial reduction in AOM incidence among infants aged < 12 months, suggesting that RSV immunisation may reduce the burden of AOM in early childhood. WHAT'S KNOWN: • RSV is a major cause of morbidity during infancy, and acute otitis media is among its most frequent complications. • Nirsevimab has demonstrated high efficacy in preventing severe RSV disease in young children; however, its effect on outpatient RSV-related complications has not been well established. WHAT IS NEW: • This study provides population-based real-world evidence on the impact of nirsevimab on acute otitis media. • Following the implementation of nirsevimab prophylaxis, the incidence of acute otitis media among infants decreased significantly.

Following nirsevimab implementation, the incidence of AOM and RSV among infants aged < 12 months decreased by 44% (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.54-0.58) and 83% (RR 0.17, 95% CI 0.15-0.18), respectively. The reduction was greatest in the youngest age (0-2 months) group. CONCLUSION: Implementation of a nirsevimab immunisation programme was associated with a substantial reduction in AOM incidence among infants aged < 12 months, suggesting that RSV immunisation may reduce the burden of AOM in early childhood. WHAT'S KNOWN: • RSV is a major cause of morbidity during infancy, and acute otitis media is among its most frequent complications. • Nirsevimab has demonstrated high efficacy in preventing severe RSV disease in young children; however, its effect on outpatient RSV-related complications has not been well established. WHAT IS NEW: • This study provides population-based real-world evidence on the impact of nirsevimab on acute otitis media. • Following the implementation of nirsevimab prophylaxis, the incidence of acute otitis media among infants decreased significantly.

full_text: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a machine learning–based model to accurately classify the risk of severe pneumonia in children infected with hMPV. Methods This retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled clinical data from 854 hospitalized children with hMPV-associated pneumonia at Kunming Children’s Hospital between December 2019 and March 2025. According to guideline-based criteria, patients were classified into a severe pneumonia group (n = 203) and a non-severe pneumonia group (n = 651). The dataset was randomly divided into a training set and a testing set at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Six machine learning models, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, naïve Bayes, multilayer perceptron, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were constructed and compared in the training set. Model performance in the independent testing set was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Clinical net benefit was assessed using decision curve analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were applied to visually interpret the optimal model. Results LASSO regression identified 9 core predictors: age, wheezing, pulmonary rales, pleural effusion, ferritin, lactate dehydrogenase, neutrophil percentage, neutrophil count, and albumin. Among the six models, XGBoost and logistic regression demonstrated comparable overall performance. XGBoost achieved a training set AUC of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.84–0.90) and a test set AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.72–0.85). The accuracy on the training set was 0.81, the sensitivity was 0.99, the specificity was 0.23, and the F1 score was 0.89; the accuracy on the test set was 0.79, the sensitivity was 0.98, the specificity was 0.17, and the F1 score was 0.88.Decision curve analysis indicated that the model provided a favorable clinical net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis revealed that wheezing, age, and pulmonary rales were the three most influential predictors. Conclusion We successfully developed and validated machine learning models, particularly XGBoost and logistic regression, for risk classification of severe pneumonia in children with hMPV infection. The model demonstrated strong discriminative performance, clinical utility, and interpretability, and may serve as a valuable decision-support tool for risk stratification of high-risk pediatric patients. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性队列研究研究于2019年12月至2025年3月在昆明儿童医院开展,纳入了854名因人偏肺病毒(hMPV)相关肺炎而住院的儿童,并将其分为重症肺炎组和非重症肺炎组。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用了一种机器学习方法,包括使用LASSO回归进行特征选择,并在训练集上比较了六个模型(逻辑回归、k近邻、朴素贝叶斯、多层感知机、随机森林和XGBoost),使用AUC、准确率、灵敏度、特异性和F1分数在测试集上评估模型性能。
elements_zh.main_results: XGBoost和逻辑回归模型表现出相当的性能,XGBoost在训练集和测试集上的AUC分别为0.87(95% CI:0.84–0.90)和0.78(95% CI:0.72–0.85)。SHAP分析确定喘息、年龄和肺部啰音是最具影响力的预测因子。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究成功开发并验证了用于人偏肺病毒感染儿童严重肺炎风险分类的机器学习模型,特别是XGBoost和逻辑回归模型,展示了强大的判别性能和临床应用价值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些模型可能作为有价值的决策支持工具,用于高风险儿科患者人偏肺病毒感染的风险分层,有助于临床决策和资源分配。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其回顾性设计和单一医院的限制,这可能会影响其结果的普遍适用性。样本量适中,且模型未与其他已建立的方法进行比较。

abstract_zh: 方法 本项回顾性队列研究研究连续纳入了2019年12月至2025年3月期间昆明儿童医院收治的854例与人偏肺病毒(hMPV)相关的肺炎患儿的临床数据。结果 基于LASSO回归,确定了9个核心预测因子:年龄、喘息、肺部湿啰音、胸腔积液、铁蛋白、乳酸脱氢酶、中性粒细胞百分比、中性粒细胞计数和白蛋白。结论 我们成功开发并验证了基于机器学习的模型,特别是XGBoost和逻辑回归模型,用于对hMPV感染儿童严重肺炎风险进行分类。伦理声明 伦理批准和参与同意 本研究已获得昆明医科大学儿童医院伦理审查委员会的批准。由于本研究为回顾性设计,昆明医科大学儿童医院伦理审查委员会(KMSETYY-IIT-2025-002(GC))豁免了知情同意的要求。此外,所有方法均按照相关指南和法规或赫尔辛基宣言进行。摘要 目的 开发并验证一个基于机器学习的模型,以准确分类hMPV感染儿童严重肺炎的风险。根据基于指南的标准,患者被分为严重肺炎组(n = 203)和非严重肺炎组(n = 651)。数据集以7:3的比例随机分为训练集和测试集。使用最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归进行特征选择。包括逻辑回归、k近邻、朴素贝叶斯、多层感知机、随机森林和极端梯度提升在内的六种机器学习模型被用于分析。
summary_zh: 方法 本项回顾性队列研究研究连续纳入了2019年12月至2025年3月期间昆明儿童医院收治的854例与人偏肺病毒(hMPV)相关的肺炎患儿的临床数据。结果 基于LASSO回归,确定了9个核心预测因子:年龄、喘息、肺部湿啰音、胸腔积液、铁蛋白、乳酸脱氢酶、中性粒细胞百分比、中性粒细胞计数和白蛋白。结论 我们成功开发并验证了基于机器学习的模型,特别是XGBoost和逻辑回归模型,用于对hMPV感染儿童严重肺炎风险进行分类。伦理声明 伦理批准和参与同意 本研究已获得昆明医科大学儿童医院伦理审查委员会的批准。由于本研究为回顾性设计,昆明医科大学儿童医院伦理审查委员会(KMSETYY-IIT-2025-002(GC))豁免了知情同意的要求。此外,所有方法均按照相关指南和法规或赫尔辛基宣言进行。摘要 目的 开发并验证一个基于机器学习的模型,以准确分类hMPV感染儿童严重肺炎的风险。根据基于指南的标准,患者被分为严重肺炎组(n = 203)和非严重肺炎组(n = 651)。数据集以7:3的比例随机分为训练集和测试集。使用最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归进行特征选择。包括逻辑回归、k近邻、朴素贝叶斯、多层感知机、随机森林和极端梯度提升在内的六种机器学习模型被用于分析。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发并验证一种机器学习模型,以准确分类人偏肺病毒(hMPV)感染儿童发生严重肺炎的风险,以应对在此背景下对更优诊断工具的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性队列研究研究于2019年12月至2025年3月在昆明儿童医院开展,纳入了854名因人偏肺病毒(hMPV)相关肺炎而住院的儿童,并将其分为重症肺炎组和非重症肺炎组。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究采用了一种机器学习方法,包括使用LASSO回归进行特征选择,并在训练集上比较了六个模型(逻辑回归、k近邻、朴素贝叶斯、多层感知机、随机森林和XGBoost),使用AUC、准确率、灵敏度、特异性和F1分数在测试集上评估模型性能。
analysis_zh.main_results: XGBoost和逻辑回归模型表现出相当的性能,XGBoost在训练集和测试集上的AUC分别为0.87(95% CI:0.84–0.90)和0.78(95% CI:0.72–0.85)。SHAP分析确定喘息、年龄和肺部啰音是最具影响力的预测因子。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究成功开发并验证了用于人偏肺病毒感染儿童严重肺炎风险分类的机器学习模型,特别是XGBoost和逻辑回归模型,展示了强大的判别性能和临床应用价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些模型可能作为有价值的决策支持工具,用于高风险儿科患者人偏肺病毒感染的风险分层,有助于临床决策和资源分配。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其回顾性设计和单一医院的限制,这可能会影响其结果的普遍适用性。样本量适中,且模型未与其他已建立的方法进行比较。

full_text: AbstractIntroductionAvian metapneumovirus subtype C (aMPV/C), a re-emerging and widespread epidemic in China, causes hydrosalpinx fluid syndrome (HFS) in laying ducks, resulting in significant economic losses to the poultry industry. In the absence of any licensed vaccines or antiviral drugs for aMPV/C, accurate diagnosis and timely eradication of the infected ducks remain the primary control measures, underscoring the urgent need for reliable and effective detection methods.MethodsIn this study, the purified whole novel aMPV/C was used to develop an indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (iELISA) for the detection of aMPV/C antibodies in ducks.ResultsThe cut-off value of the iELISA was determined to be 0.258. No cross-reactivity was observed with duck sera positive for antibodies against H5 AIV, NDV, DTMUV, BTV, DHAV-3, DPV, EDSV, MDPV, or GPV, demonstrating good specificity. Both intra-assay and inter-assay coefficients of variation were less than 10%, and the detection sensitivity of the iELISA reached a serum dilution of 1:102400. A total of 216 clinical serum samples from three duck breeds were tested via the established iELISA, of which 129 (59.7%) were positive. The concordance rate between the iELISA and an indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) was 100% (53/53).ConclusionOverall, this cost-effective iELISA provides a reliable tool for the detection of aMPV/C antibodies in clinical diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance.Keywords: avian metapneumovirus subtype C, novel, ducks, indirect ELISA, serological detection Materials and methodsVirus purificationThe aMPV/C isolate (aMPV-FJ21, 106.56 TCID50/mL) maintained in our laboratory was used in this study (Fu et al., 2025). Vero cells were inoculated with the virus, maintained in serum-free medium, and harvested at 96 h post-infection (hpi), followed by storage at −70 °C. The harvested cells were subjected to three cycles of freezing and thawing. The virus was then inactivated with 0.1% formaldehyde at 37 °C overnight. For antigen purification, 300 mL of inactivated suspension was clarified by centrifugation at 10000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C to remove cellular debris. Subsequently, the virus suspension was pelleted by ultracentrifugation at 45000 × g for 5 h. The resulting pellet was resuspended in 1 mL of 0.01 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH7.4) and used as the coating antigen for ELISA development. Meanwhile, the purified virus was examined using a transmission electron microscope (TEM, H-7500, Hitachi, Japan). And its protein concentration was determined using the enhanced BCA protein assay kit (Beyotime Biotechnology China, Fuzhou, China).Generation of polyclonal antibody against aMPV/CPurified aMPV-FJ21 strain, emulsified with an equal volume of Freund’s complete adjuvant (Sigma-Aldrich, Kenilworth, United States), was used as the immunogen for polyclonal antibody production. Sheldrake ducks were immunized with 1 mL immunogen via multiple subcutaneous injections in the dorsal region, with a negative control group included in parallel. Immunizations were administered at 2-week intervals for a total of four doses. The primary immunization used Freund’s complete adjuvant, whereas the three subsequent booster doses employed Freund’s incomplete adjuvant. Serum samples were collected 2 weeks after the final immunization for subsequent analysis.Establishment of the whole aMPV/C virus-based iELISACheckerboard titrationOptimal iELISA conditions were determined by checkerboard titration. Briefly, 96-well plates (Corning, New York, United States) were coated with 100 μL/well of purified aMPV-FJ21 at concentrations of 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 and 0.5 μg/mL in carbonate buffer (CBS, 0.05 M, pH 9.6) at 37 °C for 1 h. After three washes with PBS containing 0.05% (v/v) Tween 20 (PBST), plates were blocked with 10% skimmed milk in PBS at 37 °C for 2 h, followed by three additional washes. aMPV/C-positive and aMPV/C-negative duck sera, serially diluted from 1:100 to 1:3200 in PBS, were added (100 μL/well) and incubated at 37 °C for 1 h. Plates were washed, and 100 μL of horseradish peroxidase-conjugated goat anti-duck IgG antibody (1:10000, KPL, Maryland, United States) was added, followed by incubation at 37 °C for 1 h. After washing, 100 μL of TMB substrate (Solarbio, Beijing, China) was added and incubated at 37 °C for 10 min. The reaction was stopped with 50 μL/well of stop solution, and the optical density was measured at 450 nm (OD450nm) using an automatic ELISA reader (SpectraMax M3, Molecular Devices, USA). The optimal conditions were selected based on the highest positive-to-negative (P/N) ratio.Optimization of experimental parametersTo determine optimal coating conditions, different coating times (overnight at 4 °C; 1, 2 and 3 h at 37 °C) and coating solutions (normal saline, PBS, CBS, and ddH2O) were evaluated. The iELISA was then performed to optimize blocking times (60, 90, 120, and 150 min at 37 °C) and blocking solutions (1, 2% BSA, 5, 10% skimmed milk, and 10% FBS). Next, antibody–antigen reaction times, various incubation periods (30, 60, 90, and 120 min at 37 °C) and dilutions of the enzyme-labeled secondary antibody (1:2000, 1:4000, 1:5000, 1:8000, and 1:10000) were tested. Finally, TMB reaction times (5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 min at 37 °C) was evaluated to identify the optimal assay conditions.Determination of the cut-off valueTo determine the cut-off value for the iELISA, 57 serum samples from healthy ducks (negative for aMPV/C) were used. The cut-off was calculated based on the mean and standard deviation (SD) of the OD450nm values obtained from negative samples. It was defined as the mean OD450nm of the 57 negative sera plus 3SD, a threshold that theoretically provides >99% confidence that results from true negative samples fell below this value.Specificity and repeatabilityThe specificity of the iELISA was evaluated using positive sera against H5 avian influenza virus (H5 AIV, titer: 7log2), Newcastle disease virus (NDV, titer: 6log2), egg drop syndrome virus (EDSV, titer: 6log2), duck Tembusu virus (DTMUV, titer: 1:512), duck plague virus (DPV, titer: 1:640), Batai virus (BTV, titer: 1:256), Muscovy duck parvovirus (MDPV, titer: 1:512), goose parvovirus (GPV, titer: 1:640), and duck hepatitis A virus type 3 (DHAV-3, titer: 1:1024). Antibody titers against H5 AIV, NDV, and EDSV were assessed using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay, whereas titers against DTMUV, DPV, BTV, MDPV, GPV, and DHAV-3 were evaluated by iELISA. aMPV/C-positive and aMPV/C-negative sera were included as controls.To assess the repeatability of the iELISA, four aMPV/C-positive and four aMPV/C-negative sera were randomly selected and tested in triplicate on both the same batch and different batches of ELISA plates. Variability was expressed as the coefficient of variation (CV), calculated as the standard deviation (SD) divided by the mean optical density at OD450nm for each sample group.Sensitivity of the iELISAThe sensitivity of the iELISA was evaluated using twofold serial dilutions of three aMPV/C-positive serum with different OD450nm, ranging from 1:100 to 1:204800, in a parallel assay.IFAThe viral antigen was detected by IFA during this period as described by Fu et al. (2025). Briefly, Vero cells in 96-well plates (105 cells/well) were infected with the aMPV-FJ21 strain (105TCID50) for 72 h. Following infection, cells were fixed with pre-cooled 4% paraformaldehyde (Sigma-Aldrich, Kenilworth, USA) in PBS for 15 min at 4 °C and permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100 (Sigma-Aldrich, Kenilworth, USA) in PBS containing 2% BSA (Beyotime, Shanghai, China) for 30 min. The fixed cells were then incubated with test serum (1:100) as the primary antibody for 1.5 h at 37 °C. aMPV/C-negative serum served as a mock control. After washing with PBST, the cells were incubated with Alexa Fluor 488-labeled goat anti-duck IgG (1:200, KPL, Maryland, United States) for 1 h at 37 °C. Finally, all samples were observed under a Nikon A1R confocal fluorescence microscope (Nikon Instruments, Inc., Melville, United States).Detection of antibodies in clinical serum samplesA total of 216 clinical serum samples from ducks exhibiting a drop in egg production or respiratory symptoms, comprising 136 from Sheldrake ducks, 42 from Muscovy ducks, and 38 from Cherry Valley ducks, were tested using the established iELISA. Subsequently, 53 of these samples were randomly selected for detection by IFA, and the concordance rate between the two methods was calculated.Statistical analysisEach experiment was carried out in at least three independent replicates. Significant differences were determined using t-tests and non-parametric tests in GraphPad 8.0, with a significance level set of p < 0.05. ResultsVirus purification and identificationThe harvested virions were further purified by ultracentrifugation and TEM revealed that the virions exhibited irregular, spherical, and long filamentous morphologies, with some filamentous particles reaching approximately 1,000 nm in length (Figure 1). This morphology was consistent with the characteristic appearance of aMPV/C, confirming the successful purification of intact virions. The concentration of the purified virus was 2.05 mg/mL determined by BCA.Figure 1The electron micrograph of the purified aMPV-FJ21. Spherical, irregular, long filamentous and enveloped particles (20 nm ~ 500 nm in diameter) were observed.Transmission electron microscope image showing several rod-shaped bacteria scattered in various orientations, with a scale bar indicating 500 nanometers and cellular structures appearing as dark areas against a lighter background.Development of iELISA for detection of aMPV/C antibodiesAn iELISA was developed for aMPV/C antibody detection, and all reaction conditions were systematically optimized. The optimal coating antigen concentration as determined by checkerboard titration was 4 μg/mL, and the optimal serum dilution was identified as 1:1600 (Figure 2A). For coating and blocking, the optimal protocol consisted of coating with CBS for 1 h at 37 °C (Figures 2B,C) and blocking with 10% skimmed milk for 90 min at 37 °C (Figures 2D,E). Further optimization established the following conditions: 60-min serum incubation (Figure 2F), a secondary antibody dilution of 1:4000 with a 60-min incubation (Figures 2G,H), and a 20-min TMB (Figure 2I).Figure 2Optimization of working conditions of the established iELISA. (A) The optimal concentration of the coating antigen and the dilution duck serumdetermined via the checkerboard titration. (B,C) Determination of the optimal coating buffer and condition. (D,E) Determination of optimal blocking buffer and time. (F) Determination of the antigen–antibody incubation time. (G,H) Optimization of secondary antibody dilution and reaction time. (I) Optimal incubation time of TMB.Panel A shows a heatmap with x-axis representing serum dilution factors and y-axis representing antigen concentration, with intensity indicating signal strength. Panels B to I display bar and line combination charts analyzing variables affecting ELISA performance: coating buffer, coating condition, blocking buffer, blocking time, antigen-antibody reaction time, secondary antibody dilution, secondary antibody incubation, and TMB substrate incubation, with y-axes for OD values and positive/negative ratios, and x-axes for experimental conditions.Cut-off values for the iELISATo establish the cut-off value for the iELISA, 57 healthy duck serum samples were tested. The mean OD450nm value of the negative samples was 0.123, with a SD of 0.045. Based on these data, the cut-off value was set at 0.258 (mean + 3SD). Accordingly, serum samples with an OD450nm value≥0.258 were considered positive for aMPV/C antibodies, whereas those with values below this threshold were classified as negative (Figure 3).Figure 3Determination of the cut-off value in iELISA method. A total of 57 negative sera were detected via the iELISA and the cut-off value was set at 0.258 (mean + 3SD).Scatter plot showing individual OD four hundred fifty nanometer values as black dots, with horizontal lines indicating mean and standard deviation. Mean is zero point one two three, standard deviation is zero point zero four five.Specificity, reproducibility, and sensitivity of iELISASpecificity testing showed that only aMPV/C-positive sera reacted in the iELISA, whereas sera against H5 AIV, NDV, EDSV, DTMUV, DPV, BTV, MDPV, GPV, and DHAV-3 were all negative (Figure 4A). Repeatability was assessed using eight selected serum samples. Inter-assay CVs ranged from 1.42 to 4.48%, and intra-assay CVs ranged from 1.28 to 6.74%, both below the acceptable threshold of 10% (Table 1), indicating excellent reproducibility. Sensitivity was determined by testing three aMPV/C-positive sera in twofold serial dilutions from 1:100 to 1:204800. The highest dilution yielding a positive signal was 1:102400 (Figure 4B). These results demonstrate that the iELISA exhibits high specificity, reproducibility, and sensitivity for detecting aMPV/C antibodies.Figure 4Cross reaction and detection limit of the iELISA. (A) The cross-reactions of the iELISA were assessed by detecting 10 sera against common duck viruses. (B) The lowest detection limit of the iELISA was determined by serial dilutions of three duck aMPV/C-positive serum samples.Bar graph comparing OD450 nanometer values for ten virus types with a red dotted line indicating a cut-off value of 0.258; N-aMPV/C shows a significantly higher bar than all others, which are below the cut-off.Table 1Results of the repeatability test of the iELISA.Serum samplesIntra-assayInter-assayMean ± SDCV (%)Mean ± SDCV (%)Positive serum 12.127 ± 0.0954.48%2.145 ± 0.0622.90%Positive serum 22.447 ± 0.0743.01%2.486 ± 0.0491.95%Positive serum 32.245 ± 0.0321.42%2.271 ± 0.0291.28%Positive serum 42.315 ± 0.0622.69%2.364 ± 0.0421.77%Negative serum 10.079 ± 0.0022.23%0.08 ± 0.0033.26%Negative serum 20.108 ± 0.0033.21%0.112 ± 0.0043.63%Negative serum 30.204 ± 0.0052.43%0.201 ± 0.0015.20%Negative serum 40.104 ± 0.0021.78%0.101 ± 0.0076.74%Detection of antibodies in clinical serum samplesA total of 216 duck serum samples were analyzed using the established iELISA, with results validated by IFA (Figure 5). As presented in Table 2, the positivity rate was highest in Sheldrake ducks (69.1%, 94/136), followed by Muscovy ducks (57.1%, 24/42) and Cherry Valley ducks (28.9%, 11/38), resulting in an overall seroprevalence of 59.7% (129/216). Furthermore, among 53 randomly selected samples, 45 were concordantly identified as aMPV/C-positive and 8 were negative by iELISA and IFA (Table 3). The concordance rate between the two detection methods was 100% (53/53), indicating that the iELISA is a reliable and rapid tool for clinical diagnosis.Figure 5Detection of duck serum samples by IFA. (A–C) Vero cells infected with aMPV-FJ21 showed green fluorescence when incubated with anti-aMPV/C-positive duck sera. (D–F) No fluorescence signal was detected with negative sera.Six-panel fluorescence microscopy figure showing three rows labeled DAPI, FITC, and MERGE. Panels A and D display blue-stained nuclei. Panel B shows green fluorescence in many cells. Panel C merges blue and green signals, revealing overlap. Panel E is blank, and panel F resembles D with only blue-stained nuclei visible. Scale bars read one hundred micrometers.Table 2Detection of aMPV/C infection in four duck breeds via iELISA.Duck breedsNumber of tested samplesNumber of positive samplesPositivity rate (%)Sheldrake ducks1369469.1Muscovy ducks422457.1Cherry Valley ducks381128.9Total21612959.7Table 3Comparison of the self-established iELISA with IFA for detection of duck sera.Serum samplesSelf-established iELISAPositive samplesNegative samplesTotalPositive samples tested by IFA45045Negative samples tested by IFA088Total45853Coincidence rate100% DiscussionSince Although aMPV subtype B has historically been the dominant lineage in Chinese poultry, the epidemiological landscape has shifted considerably since 2021, with aMPV/C now emerging as a significant pathogen in domestic duck populations (Fu et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2022). This epidemiological transition is particularly noteworthy given that aMPV/C was first detected in ducks in 2014 but remained largely unreported in waterfowl for nearly a decade, suggesting that the virus may have undergone adaptive changes that facilitated its spread and establishment in duck hosts (Sun et al., 2014). The recent identification of a novel aMPV/C lineage in Sheldrake ducks is especially concerning, as this variant appears to have acquired a distinct tropism for reproductive tissues, manifesting as hydrosalpinx fluid syndrome rather than the classical respiratory disease typically associated with aMPV infections (Fu et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2024). This clinical shift from respiratory to reproductive pathology may reflect ongoing viral evolution and adaptation to new host species, potentially involving changes in the viral attachment protein or other surface glycoproteins that determine cell tropism. Furthermore, the seasonal recurrence of this disease on affected farms, often correlated with annual climatic variations, complicates disease control efforts and underscores the urgent need for diagnostic tools that are both reliable and broadly applicable across different duck breeds and production systems (Fu et al., 2025; Sun et al., 2014).Historically, aMPV subtypes A, B, and C have predominantly circulated in chickens and turkeys worldwide (Cook, 2000; Salles et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2013). Sheldrake ducks were immunized with 1 mL immunogen via multiple subcutaneous injections in the dorsal region, with a negative control group included in parallel. Briefly, 96-well plates (Corning, New York, United States) were coated with 100 μL/well of purified aMPV-FJ21 at concentrations of 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 and 0.5 μg/mL in carbonate buffer (CBS, 0.05 M, pH 9.6) at 37 °C for 1 h. Plates were washed, and 100 μL of horseradish peroxidase-conjugated goat anti-duck IgG antibody (1:10000, KPL, Maryland, United States) was added, followed by incubation at 37 °C for 1 h. The reaction was stopped with 50 μL/well of stop solution, and the optical density was measured at 450 nm (OD450nm) using an automatic ELISA reader (SpectraMax M3, Molecular Devices, USA). The optimal conditions were selected based on the highest positive-to-negative (P/N) ratio.Optimization of experimental parametersTo determine optimal coating conditions, different coating times (overnight at 4 °C; 1, 2 and 3 h at 37 °C) and coating solutions (normal saline, PBS, CBS, and ddH2O) were evaluated. full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionSince Although aMPV subtype B has historically been the dominant lineage in Chinese poultry, the epidemiological landscape has shifted considerably since 2021, with aMPV/C now emerging as a significant pathogen in domestic duck populations (Fu et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2022). This epidemiological transition is particularly noteworthy given that aMPV/C was first detected in ducks in 2014 but remained largely unreported in waterfowl for nearly a decade, suggesting that the virus may have undergone adaptive changes that facilitated its spread and establishment in duck hosts (Sun et al., 2014). The recent identification of a novel aMPV/C lineage in Sheldrake ducks is especially concerning, as this variant appears to have acquired a distinct tropism for reproductive tissues, manifesting as hydrosalpinx fluid syndrome rather than the classical respiratory disease typically associated with aMPV infections (Fu et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2024). This clinical shift from respiratory to reproductive pathology may reflect ongoing viral evolution and adaptation to new host species, potentially involving changes in the viral attachment protein or other surface glycoproteins that determine cell tropism. Furthermore, the seasonal recurrence of this disease on affected farms, often correlated with annual climatic variations, complicates disease control efforts and underscores the urgent need for diagnostic tools that are both reliable and broadly applicable across different duck breeds and production systems (Fu et al., 2025; Sun et al., 2014).Historically, aMPV subtypes A, B, and C have predominantly circulated in chickens and turkeys worldwide (Cook, 2000; Salles et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2013). Consequently, numerous indirect ELISAs using various structural proteins (N, M, F, and G) as coating antigens have been developed for serological surveillance in these species (Chiang et al., 2000; Gulati et al., 2000; Gulati et al., 2001; Alvarez et al., 2004; Xu et al., 2021). However, no commercial ELISA kit is currently available for detecting aMPV antibodies in duck sera, particularly against subtype C. To address this diagnostic gap, we developed an iELISA using whole inactivated aMPV/C virions as the coating antigen. This approach offers distinct advantages over recombinant protein-based assays, which have been the standard for aMPV serology in chickens and turkeys. While recombinant proteins are widely adopted due to their ease of production and scalability, they often fail to present the full repertoire of conformational and linear epitopes present on native viral particles, and interference from components of the prokaryotic expression host (Escherichia coli), potentially compromising assay sensitivity and leading to false-negative results, especially in low-titer samples (Meireles et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2026). In contrast, whole-virion antigens preserve the native antigenic architecture, enabling more comprehensive detection across a broader range of antibody specificities and isotypes (Sumita et al., 2016). This feature is particularly valuable for detecting antibodies against emerging viral variants, as a single recombinant protein may not adequately capture the antigenic diversity of circulating strains. The aMPV-FJ21 strain used in this study achieved high titers in Vero cells, substantially exceeding previously reported levels at the same passage, thereby providing ample antigen for large-scale production while ensuring consistent quality (Sun et al., 2014; Yao et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2023). The use of a single master seed stock, combined with serum-free culture conditions and rigorous control of passage number and culture parameters, further ensured batch- to-batch consistency and minimized the risk of exogenous protein contamination that could otherwise compromise assay specificity.The analytical performance of the iELISA was robust and met the requirements for a practical diagnostic tool. No cross-reactivity was observed against sera positive for nine other major duck pathogens, including H5 AIV, NDV, EDSV, DTMUV, DPV, BTV, MDPV, GPV, and DHAV-3, demonstrating high specificity. This specificity is critical for accurate diagnosis in field settings where co-infections with multiple pathogens are common. The detection limit of 1:102400 indicates high sensitivity, making the assay suitable for detecting low-titer antibodies in field samples, particularly during the early stages of infection or in vaccinated flocks where antibody levels may be relatively low. The excellent reproducibility of the assay, with coefficients of variation below 10% in both intra- and inter-assay evaluations, confirms its operational stability and reliability for routine diagnostic use across different laboratories and operators.Application of the iELISA to 216 clinical serum samples collected from three duck breeds revealed an overall seroprevalence of 59.7%, with notable variation among breeds: Sheldrake ducks showed the highest positivity rate (69.1%), followed by Muscovy ducks (57.1%) and Cherry Valley ducks (28.9%). This breed-dependent variation may reflect differences in genetic susceptibility, management practices, or environmental exposure, and warrants further investigation into the host factors that influence aMPV/C infection dynamics. The higher seroprevalence observed in Sheldrake and Muscovy ducks compared to Cherry Valley ducks could be related to breed-specific differences in receptor expression, immune response efficiency, or husbandry practices that affect virus transmission. The complete concordance (100%) between the iELISA and IFA in a subset of 53 samples further validates the reliability of the assay and supports its utility as a practical tool for large-scale serological surveillance. This high level of agreement suggests that the iELISA can be used interchangeably with IFA, offering the advantages of higher throughput, objective readout, and reduced labor intensity, making it particularly suitable for epidemiological surveys and routine monitoring programs in commercial duck farms. These findings collectively support the suitability of the developed iELISA for large-scale serological surveillance of aMPV/C infection in duck flocks, providing a valuable tool for disease monitoring and control efforts.
full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionIn summary, we developed a sensitive, specific, and reproducible iELISA for detecting aMPV/C antibodies in duck sera, demonstrating 100% concordance with IFA. This assay provides a practical tool for large-scale serological surveillance. The widespread seropositivity across duck breeds highlights the urgent need for vaccination strategies and routine monitoring to mitigate the impact of aMPV/C on China’s duck industry.
full_text_sections.other: IntroductionAvian metapneumovirus (aMPV) was first identified in South Africa in 1978 (Buys and Preez, 1980) and has since become a globally distributed pathogen, infecting both domestic poultry and wild avian species (Salles et al., 2023). The virus causes upper respiratory disease, typically characterized by sinusitis, head swelling, and decreased egg production (Clontz and Hoerr, 2026; De Graaf et al., 2009). In uncomplicated cases, mortality is generally low (2–5%); however, co-infections with secondary pathogens can elevate mortality to as high as 25%. Based on genetic and antigenic variability, aMPV is classified into four subtypes (A-D) (Juhasz and Easton, 1994; Bäyon-Auboyer et al., 2000; Rima et al., 2017). Subtypes A and B are distributed worldwide, with subtype B predominating in Europe and China (Franzo et al., 2020). Subtype C naturally infects turkeys, chickens, ducks, and wild birds, and its genome exhibits the highest homology with human metapneumovirus (Hatfield et al., 2026). Prior to 2025, aMPV/C was known to comprise two distinct lineages: the North American and the Eurasian lineages (Quan et al., 2020). Recently, our group identified a novel lineage circulating in Sheldrake ducks (Fu et al., 2025). In contrast, subtype D has only been reported in France (Umar et al., 2019). Notably, two novel and divergent aMPV strains were detected in North America in 2019, further highlighting the ongoing expansion of aMPV genetic diversity (Canuti et al., 2019; Retallack et al., 2019).In China, aMPV/C was first recorded in Muscovy ducks in 2014, with no subsequent isolations from waterfowl reported until 2021 (Sun et al., 2014). Since then, the virus has become increasingly prevalent nationwide, causing hydrosalpinx fluid syndrome (HFS) in laying ducks and respiratory disease in meat ducks (Yu et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2025). In 2025, we isolated a novel strain, designated aMPV-FJ21, from Sheldrake ducks exhibiting HFS (Fu et al., 2025). Molecular characterization revealed that this strain is genetically distinct from both the North American and Eurasian lineages, indicating ongoing genetic diversification and adaptive evolution of aMPV/C in China (Fu et al., 2025). These findings underscore the urgent need for effective control measures, particularly rapid and reliable diagnostic tools.Current diagnostic approaches for aMPV/C include pathogen isolation, molecular assays, and serological tests. Virus isolation is labor-intensive and time-consuming, and its recovery rate from clinical samples is notoriously low, reported as only 8% (2/25), rendering it impractical for routine clinical diagnosis (Kwon et al., 2010; Sun et al., 2014). Molecular methods, such as PCR, offer high specificity and sensitivity but require specialized equipment and skilled personnel (Shin et al., 2000). Moreover, their diagnostic utility is constrained by the short viremic window of aMPV/C, typically lasting only 2–10 days post-infection (Cook et al., 1993; Cook et al., 2001). Serological assays, including virus neutralization tests (VNT), IFA, and ELISA, are widely employed for antibody detection (Chiang et al., 2000). Among these, ELISA is particularly suitable for large-scale surveillance due to its high throughput, sensitivity, and specificity, and remains a cornerstone for monitoring infection pressure, assessing flock immunity, and guiding vaccination strategies (Saeed et al., 2026). However, to date, no commercial ELISA kit is available for the detection of aMPV/C antibodies in duck sera.To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed an iELISA using a purified novel aMPV/C isolate as the coating antigen, specifically designed for the detection of aMPV/C antibodies in duck sera. full_text: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. The summer peak of HBoV and the seasonally independent climatic drivers of RSV and HMPV provide a preliminary basis that, if confirmed with higher-resolution data, could inform pathogen-tailored, climate-informed surveillance in northern Chinese megacities. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting and populationWe conducted a retrospective single-center surveillance study at the Department of Respiratory Medicine, Tianjin Children’s Hospital (Ma-Chang campus), the only tertiary-A comprehensive children’s hospital in Tianjin. The hospital is the principal pediatric referral center for Tianjin municipality and, for selected specialties, draws patients from across the wider North China Plain; publicly reported hospital-wide figures indicate roughly 17,000–20,000 pediatric admissions per year across all departments. Our cohort of 2,597 virologically confirmed viral LRTI cases represents the subset of hospitalized LRTI cases that were both tested and found positive for one of the six target viruses, not the total burden of pediatric LRTI hospitalization in Tianjin. A precise, denominator-based estimate of the proportion of all Tianjin pediatric LRTI hospitalizations captured by this cohort is not available, because no citywide pediatric LRTI hospitalization registry exists for comparison. As a tertiary referral center, the cohort is likely enriched for more severe disease and for cases referred from primary and secondary facilities; this referral pattern, and the resulting limit on generalizability to primary care, is revisited in the Discussion (Section 4.6).Eligible participants were children aged 0–18 years hospitalized with a clinical diagnosis of LRTI between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025, from whom a respiratory specimen was submitted for routine viral testing. LRTI was defined clinically, following the 2019 Chinese Pediatric Society guideline for community-acquired pneumonia (Subspecialty Group of Respiratory Diseases, 2019), as cough or fever (axillary temperature ≥38 °C) together with at least one of: tachypnoea, wheezing, crackles on auscultation, or imaging evidence of pneumonia or bronchiolitis. This definition captures the clinical syndromes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis and excludes isolated upper respiratory tract infection. We excluded children with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease, congenital airway malformations, documented immunodeficiency, active malignancy, or concurrent infection by pathogens outside the predefined six-virus panel. This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. For viruses prone to subclinical carriage, chiefly HRV and HBoV, a detection was considered clinically causative only when the tNGS reporting algorithm assigned a pathogenicity Class A grade, the clinical picture matched the corresponding viral syndrome, and other plausible infectious causes had been clinically excluded (residual misclassification risk for these two viruses is discussed in Section 4.6). For descriptive analyses, children were stratified a priori into four age categories: infants (<1 year), toddlers (1–2 years), preschoolers (3–5 years) and school-aged children (≥6 years). All records were de-identified before analysis. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Tianjin Children’s Hospital (approval number 2024-LXKY-023); written informed consent was waived given the retrospective design and full de-identification of the dataset.2.2Pathogen detectionRespiratory specimens (sputum, the predominant type; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF; nasopharyngeal swabs; and oropharyngeal swabs) were collected following standardized clinical protocols, placed into viral transport medium, and transported within two hours at 2–8 °C to the clinical laboratory. Total nucleic acids were extracted on an automated platform following the manufacturer’s instructions. All specimens were tested with the same commercial targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) panel, which simultaneously screens for respiratory bacteria, viruses, atypical pathogens and antimicrobial-resistance markers. Library construction, ultra-multiplex amplification of pathogen-specific genomic regions and Illumina-compatible high-throughput sequencing were performed following the manufacturer’s recommended workflow, with reads aligned against a curated pathogen reference database (Li et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025). The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. Monthly counts of tNGS requests could not be retrieved from the laboratory information system for the whole study window, so this account of testing volume rests on the laboratory’s implementation record rather than on an auditable series of test counts, and it should be read as such.The grade is a composite call rather than a single read-count cut-off. It is generated by an integrated scoring system that combines normalized read counts (reads per million, RPM), the breadth of genome coverage achieved across the targeted regions, and species-level annotation of pathogenicity against a curated reference database; Class A is assigned to organisms that meet the pre-specified RPM and coverage criteria for a clinically significant pathogen. The numerical RPM and coverage cut-offs behind the grade are proprietary to the assay vendor and are not released to the ordering laboratory; we are therefore unable to report them, and the grade as issued was the only form in which this information was available to us. Grading was prospective in the sense that it was performed by the clinical laboratory at the time the routine diagnostic report was issued and used for patient care, and the research team did not re-adjudicate the classifications retrospectively. No Class A detection was subsequently excluded on the grounds of clinical mismatch, because the Class A flag served as an inclusion criterion for the six-virus panel rather than as the sole determinant of clinical causality; for HRV and HBoV, the additional clinical adjudication described in Section 2.1 was applied instead.The full panel detects a broader range of organisms than the six viruses analyzed here. Common bacterial pathogens reported by the full panel include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus; the atypical pathogens include Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia pneumoniae; and respiratory viruses outside the six-virus panel, including parainfluenza viruses, seasonal coronaviruses and SARS-CoV-2, are likewise covered. Consistent with the eligibility criteria set out in Section 2.1, a child in whom any of these organisms was reported concurrently with one of the six target viruses was excluded from the cohort at screening rather than merely omitted from the analysis; the cases analysed here are therefore restricted to children whose Class A detections fell entirely within the six-virus panel. We restricted the present analysis to the six respiratory viruses (HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, IFV, covering both influenza A and B, and HMPV) flagged at the highest pathogenicity grade (Class A), for three reasons. First, these six viruses are the pathogens for which pathogen-specific climatic drivers are most biologically plausible and best characterized, allowing direct comparison with prior lagged-climate studies (Baker et al., 2019; Li et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2021). Second, restricting to Class A calls minimizes the inclusion of low-confidence or incidental detections. Third, bacterial and atypical pathogens are subject to different detection biases (for example, antibiotic pretreatment and colonization) and different climate–transmission mechanisms, and were therefore outside the scope of this analysis. Co-infections, defined as concurrent Class A detection of two or more of the six target viruses in the same specimen, were identified and are described in Section 2.4.2.3Meteorological dataMonthly city-wide meteorological summaries for Tianjin from January 2023 to December 2025 (n = 36 months) were obtained from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau and comprised mean atmospheric pressure (hPa), mean wind speed (m/s), mean air temperature (°C), mean relative humidity (%), precipitation (mm) and mean daily sunshine duration (hours). Routine quality assurance included unit verification and column-order auditing across reporting periods. The meteorological series was time-aligned with the monthly aggregated viral case counts before analysis.We used monthly rather than daily or weekly data because the records available from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau for this study period were supplied at monthly resolution; daily or weekly city-wide summaries were not accessible for the full 2023–2025 window. Finer (for example, weekly) resolution would allow more precise estimation of short-lag effects and is standard in DLNM-based climate–infection studies (Gasparrini et al., 2010; Li et al., 2025); we discuss this resolution constraint further in Section 4.6.2.4Statistical analysisCategorical data are presented as counts (percentages) and compared between groups with Pearson’s χ2 test; the assumption of an equal sex ratio was tested with the exact binomial test, and inter-pathogen age differences with the Kruskal–Wallis test. Daily case records were aggregated to monthly totals and merged with the meteorological time series. Yates’ continuity correction was applied to 2 × 2 comparisons.Co-infections were tabulated separately from the mono-infection pathogen spectrum. The primary pathogen-spectrum analysis (case counts, proportions, and demographic and specimen-type distributions in Section 3.1) attributes each specimen to a single, mutually exclusive pathogen row, so the per-pathogen counts in Table 1 sum to the total of 2,597 virus-positive cases; co-infection structure itself (pairwise combinations, and multiplicity) is tabulated separately, with each co-infected specimen contributing to every virus it carried, and is described in Section 3.4.Table 1Demographic and specimen characteristics of pediatric viral LRTI cases by pathogen.PathogenN (% of all positive)Male, n (%)Female, n (%)Sex p-valueAge, median (IQR), yLower respiratory tract specimen, n (%)HRV796 (30.7)471 (59.2)325 (40.8)<0.0014.0 (2.0–6.0)660 (82.9)ADV692 (26.6)425 (61.4)267 (38.6)<0.0016.0 (3.0–8.0)485 (70.1)RSV536 (20.6)304 (56.7)232 (43.3)0.0023.0 (1.0–4.0)454 (84.7)HBoV313 (12.1)179 (57.2)134 (42.8)0.0132.0 (1.0–4.0)277 (88.5)IFV155 (6.0)83 (53.5)72 (46.5)0.425.0 (2.0–7.0)123 (79.4)HMPV105 (4.0)66 (62.9)39 (37.1)0.0114.0 (1.8–6.0)74 (70.5)Pathogen counts are mutually exclusive per specimen (see Section 2.4), so the column totals sum to 2,597. Co-infected specimens, in which two or more Class A viruses were detected concurrently, are tabulated separately in Section 3.4, where each such specimen contributes to the count of every virus it carried; those pairwise counts are not reflected in the totals above. Sex p-values are from the exact binomial test against a 50:50 null; age is median (IQR) in years; Lower respiratory tract specimen = sputum or BALF.Pathogen–climate co-variation was screened with Spearman’s rank correlation (ρ) on the full monthly series and re-examined within meteorological seasons (spring, March–May; summer, June–August; autumn, September–November; winter, December–February).Lagged meteorological effects were examined in two complementary ways. First, cross-correlation functions were computed over lags of 0–6 months for temperature, relative humidity and wind speed. Second, lag-specific relative risks (RR) were derived from quasi-Poisson GLMs with a log link (Bhaskaran et al., 2013; Gasparrini, 2011; Imai et al., 2015) of the form log(μt) = α + β × Xt−L, where μt is the expected monthly case count in month t and Xt−L the meteorological exposure shifted back by L months (L = 0, 1, ..., 6). Because this analysis spans 126 model fits (6 pathogens × 3 variables × 7 lags), no formal correction for multiple comparisons was applied; signals reaching p<0.01 (for example, RSV with wind speed at a 1-month lag) are interpreted as relatively robust, whereas signals in the 0.01 to 0.05 range (for example, HMPV with temperature, and RSV with temperature) are flagged as exploratory. RR values are reported per clinically interpretable unit (5 °C for temperature, 10% for relative humidity and 0.5 m/s for wind speed), each chosen to approximate the interquartile span of the corresponding variable. Standard errors were corrected for overdispersion (Pearson dispersion parameter φ ≥ 1). For every pathogen × exposure combination, the lag at which the absolute log-RR was largest among significant lags is reported as the peak RR; the resulting post-hoc selection across candidate lags is discussed as a source of potential effect-size inflation in Section 4.6.This graded reading is a descriptive convention and does not control the family-wise error rate. Under the null hypothesis, roughly six of the 126 fits would be expected to reach p<0.05 by chance, and a Bonferroni-corrected threshold would fall at p<0.0004. We report uncorrected p-values on the reasoning that the six pathogens address distinct epidemiological questions rather than a single universal null, an approach with precedent in exploratory analyses of this kind (Rothman, 1990); the accompanying Type I error risk is set out explicitly in Section 4.6. Two associations in the 0.01 to 0.05 range are nonetheless carried into the Discussion, RSV with temperature and HMPV with temperature, and both are presented there as provisional, the HMPV signal explicitly as hypothesis-generating; no clinical or public health recommendation in this paper rests on either of them alone.Because the peak RR is the largest of up to seven correlated estimates, it is biased away from the null and its confidence interval is narrower than the selection process warrants, a general property of effect estimates identified by crossing a significance threshold in underpowered analyses (Ioannidis, 2008). The complete lag profile of every pathogen × exposure combination with at least one significant lag is therefore plotted in Figure 1, and those lag-specific estimates, rather than the single peak value, should be read as the primary result.Figure 1Seasonally- and trend-adjusted relative risk (RR, 95% CI) by lag from the unified quasi-Poisson GLM, for the pathogen × climate variable combinations with at least one significant lag: RSV–temperature, RSV–wind speed, HMPV–temperature and HMPV–humidity.
